questions.question: Who appoints the Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 75** of the **Indian Constitution**, the **Prime Minister** is appointed by the **President of India**. While the President makes the formal appointment, they are bound by constitutional conventions to appoint the leader of the party or coalition that commands a **majority** in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• The **President** also appoints other **Ministers** of the Union, but this is done specifically on the **advice** of the Prime Minister.
 
• The Prime Minister serves as the **Head of the Government** and the chief link between the **Cabinet** and the President. Although the Prime Minister holds office during the **pleasure of the President**, they cannot be dismissed as long as they maintain a majority in the Lower House.
 
• Before the Prime Minister enters office, the **President** administers the **oaths of office and secrecy** as per the forms set out in the **Third Schedule** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliament**:

 
 
• Comprises the **President**, the **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States), and the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People). While it is the legislative body, it does not formally appoint the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of India**:
 
 
• The head of the **Judiciary** and the **Supreme Court**. The Chief Justice administers the oath of office to the **President** under **Article 60**, but has no role in the executive appointment of the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Vice President**:
 
 
• Functions as the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha**. According to **Article 65**, the Vice President acts as President only during casual vacancies or the President's absence.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility**:
 
 
• A person must be a member of either house of Parliament to be Prime Minister. If not a member at the time of appointment, they must be elected to either the **Lok Sabha** or **Rajya Sabha** within **six months**.

questions.question: Which article allows Parliament to amend the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 368**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 368**, located in **Part XX** of the **Constitution of India**, defines the power of **Parliament** to amend the Constitution and provides the specific procedure for such modifications.
 
• The **Parliament** may, in the exercise of its constituent power, amend by way of addition, variation, or repeal any provision of the Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down.
 
• An amendment of the Constitution can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill for the purpose in either **House of Parliament** (**Lok Sabha** or **Rajya Sabha**) and not in the **State Legislatures**.
 
• The Bill must be passed in each House by a **Special Majority**, which requires a majority of the total membership of that House and a majority of not less than **two-thirds** of the members of that House present and voting.
 
• The **Supreme Court**, in the historic **Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)**, ruled that **Parliament** cannot amend those provisions which form the **Basic Structure** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 352**

 
 
• Relates to the proclamation of a **National Emergency** by the **President** when the security of India is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
 
 
• **Article 356**
 
 
• Commonly known as **President’s Rule**, it allows for the suspension of state government and the imposition of direct central government rule in a state if the constitutional machinery fails.
 
 
 
• **Article 370**
 
 
• Formerly granted a **Temporary Special Status** to the state of **Jammu and Kashmir**; its primary provisions were rendered inoperative by a Presidential Order in **August 2019**.

questions.question: Which institution was founded by Vallathol Narayana Menon to preserve and promote Kathakali?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala Kalamandalam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Kerala Kalamandalam** was founded in **1930** by the renowned Malayalam poet **Vallathol Narayana Menon**, popularly known as **Mahakavi Vallathol**, in collaboration with **Manakkulam Mukunda Raja**.
 
• The primary objective of establishing this institution was to rescue traditional **Kerala performing arts**, particularly **Kathakali**, **Koodiyattam**, and **Mohiniyattam**, from the state of decline they had fallen into during the early 20th century.<

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the Giddha dance?

options.text: A women's folk dance involving rhythmic clapping and singing
A solo dance performed by men

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A women's folk dance involving rhythmic clapping and singing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Giddha** is a popular and **vibrant folk dance** originating from the **Punjab** region of **India** and **Pakistan**, performed exclusively by **women**.
 
• The dance is highly **rhythmic** and is characterized by its lack of heavy instrumentation; instead, the **beat** is primarily generated through **rhythmic clapping** and the use of a **Dhol** (barrel drum).
 
• It is often considered the female counterpart to the male-centric **Bhangra** dance, sharing similar energy levels but emphasizing **grace**, **femininity**, and **storytelling**.
 
• The performance involves women standing in a **circle** while singing **Boliyaan**, which are traditional **couplets** or short folk songs that reflect the **daily lives**, **emotions**, and **social experiences** of Punjabi women.
 
• One or two women usually step into the center of the circle to perform the **main dance steps** while the others provide the **chorus** and **clapping** support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cultural Significance and Occasions**:

 
 
• **Giddha** is typically performed during **festivals** such as **Baisakhi** (harvest festival) and **Teeyan** (monsoon festival dedicated to women).
 
• It is also a staple at **weddings** and other family celebrations, serving as a medium for **social bonding** and **merriment**.
 
 
 
• **Attire and Ornamentation**:
 
 
• Performers wear bright, colorful **Salwar Kameez** or **Lehengas** made of **silk** or **satin**, often heavily embroidered with **Gota-patti** or **Phulkari** work.
 
• Specific traditional **jewelry** includes the **Saggi Phul** (a floral-shaped head ornament), **Tikka**, and heavy **bangles** that add to the visual and auditory spectacle of the dance.
 
 
 
• **Thematic Content of Boliyaan**:
 
 
• The lyrics often humorously address **familial relationships**, such as the bond between a **mother-in-law** and **daughter-in-law**, or celebrate **romantic love** and **nature**.

questions.question: Which author wrote The God of Small Things?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arundhati Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arundhati Roy** is the acclaimed Indian author who wrote the semi-autobiographical novel **'The God of Small Things'**, which was published in **1997**.
 
• The novel is set in **Aymanam**, a village in the **Kottayam** district of **Kerala**, India, and follows the lives of fraternal twins, **Estha** and **Rahel**.
 
• The book gained international recognition by winning the **Man Booker Prize** for Fiction in **1997** and was cited as one of the New York Times **Notable Books of the Year**.
 
• The narrative explores complex social themes including the **caste system**, **communism**, and the rigid 'Love Laws' of Indian society, using a distinctive **non-linear timeline**.
 
• It remains one of the most significant works of **contemporary Indian literature**, having been translated into more than **40 languages** worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vikram Seth**:

 
 
• He is a renowned Indian poet and novelist, best known for his monumental novel **'A Suitable Boy'** (1993), which is one of the longest English novels ever published.
 
• His literary contributions also include **'The Golden Gate'** and **'An Equal Music'**.
 
 
 
• **Kiran Desai**:
 
 
• She is an Indian author whose novel **'The Inheritance of Loss'** won the **Man Booker Prize** in **2006**.
 
• Her writing often focuses on the themes of **post-colonialism**, **identity**, and **globalization**.
 
 
 
• **Shekhar Kapur**:
 
 
• Primarily a **film director** and producer rather than a novelist, he is famous for directing critically acclaimed movies like **'Masoom'**, **'Mr. India'**, and the Oscar-winning **'Elizabeth'**.
 
• He has served as the **Chairman** of the **Film and Television Institute of India (FTII)**.

questions.question: Which mountain range is considered the oldest in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aravalli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aravalli Range** is geologically recognized as the **oldest fold mountain** system in India and is among the oldest in the world.
 
• It originated during the **Precambrian Era**, specifically the **Proterozoic Eon**, approximately **1.8 billion years** ago, as part of the **Aravalli-Delhi Orogeny**.
 
• Today, it is categorized as a **relict mountain** or **residual mountain** because its once-towering peaks have been significantly lowered by millions of years of **weathering** and **erosion**.
 
• The range extends for about **800 kilometers** in a **Southwest-Northeast** direction, covering parts of **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, **Haryana**, and **Delhi**.
 
• The highest peak of the Aravalli range is **Guru Shikhar**, located in **Mount Abu**, reaching an elevation of **1,722 meters** above sea level.
 
• The range acts as a **climatic barrier**, preventing the eastward expansion of the **Thar Desert** and influencing the rainfall patterns in Northwest India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayas**:

 
 
• These are **Young Fold Mountains** formed during the **Cenozoic Era** (Tertiary Period) due to the collision between the **Indian Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate**.
 
• They are characterized by **high peaks**, **deep valleys**, and **fast-flowing rivers**, and they are still geologically **active** and growing.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats**:
 
 
• Also known as **Sahyadri**, this range runs parallel to the **western coast** and is older than the Himalayas but younger than the Aravallis.
 
• They represent the **faulted edge** of the **Deccan Plateau** and are a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** known for immense **biodiversity**.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Ghats**:
 
 
• A discontinuous range of mountains along India's **eastern coast** that has been eroded by major peninsular rivers like the **Godavari** and **Krishna**.
 
• While older than the Western Ghats, they were formed much later than the **Aravalli** system.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers forms Majuli, the largest riverine island?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Majuli** is a large riverine island located in the **Brahmaputra River** in the state of **Assam**, India.
 
• It was formed due to the course changes of the **Brahmaputra** and its tributaries, specifically the **Lohit River** to the north and the main **Brahmaputra** channel to the south.
 
• In **2016**, **Guinness World Records** officially designated Majuli as the **world's largest river island**, a title previously held by Marajo in Brazil.
 
• Majuli holds the unique distinction of being the first island to be made a **district** in India, a status it achieved in **September 2016**.
 
• The island is a significant site for **Neo-Vaishnavite** culture, housing numerous **Satras** (monasteries) founded by the saint-reformer **Srimanta Sankardeva**.
 
• While originally spanning over **1,200 square kilometers**, constant **soil erosion** by the Brahmaputra has reduced its current area to approximately **352 square kilometers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ganga**:

 
 
• It is the longest river in India, originating from the **Gangotri Glacier** at **Gaumukh**.
 
• Along with the Brahmaputra, it forms the **Sundarbans Delta**, which is the largest river delta in the world.
 
 
 
• **Godavari**:
 
 
• Often referred to as **Dakshin Ganga** or **Vriddh Ganga**, it is the largest peninsular river system.
 
• It originates from **Trimbakeshwar** in the **Nashik** district of Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna**:
 
 
• The largest tributary of the Ganga, it originates from the **Yamunotri Glacier** in the **Banderpooch** peaks of the Himalayas.
 
• It passes through major cities including **Delhi**, **Agra**, and **Mathura** before merging with the Ganga at **Prayagraj**.

questions.question: A student sees a rainbow just after rainfall. If he tries to move closer to the rainbow, what happens?

options.text: Rainbow appears at the same distance.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rainbow appears at the same distance.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **rainbow** is not a physical object located at a specific point in space but is an **optical phenomenon** whose perceived position depends on the **observer**.
 
• It is formed by the **refraction**, **total internal reflection**, and **dispersion** of sunlight as it passes through **spherical water droplets** in the atmosphere.
 
• The observer always sees the rainbow at a fixed **angular relationship** of approximately **40 to 42 degrees** from the **anti-solar point** (the point directly opposite the **Sun**).
 
• Because the rainbow is defined by this **angle** rather than a fixed physical coordinate, as the observer moves, the rainbow appears to move with them.
 
• When a student tries to move closer, they are simply seeing light refracted from a different set of **raindrops** that satisfy the **42-degree** viewing condition, making the rainbow appear to stay at the **same distance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dispersion**: This is the process where **white light** separates into its **spectral colors** (Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, and Violet) because different **wavelengths** refract at slightly different angles.
 
• **Anti-Solar Point**: This is the imaginary point exactly **180 degrees** opposite the Sun. The **center of the rainbow** arc is always aligned with this point.
 
• **Primary and Secondary Rainbows**:
 
 
• A **primary rainbow** involves **one internal reflection** and is brighter, with red on the outer edge.
 
• A **secondary rainbow** is caused by **two internal reflections**, appears fainter, and has a **reversed color sequence**.
 
 
 
• **Total Internal Reflection**: This occurs when the light hitting the back of the water droplet is reflected forward rather than passing through, a critical step in sending the light back toward the observer.

Therefore, the correct option is 3

questions.question: Which artist designed the stained-glass windows in the western part of St. Paul's Cathedral?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sir Edward Burne-Jones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The stained-glass windows in the **western part** of **St. Paul's Cathedral** in **Kolkata** (formerly Calcutta) were designed by the eminent **Pre-Raphaelite** artist **Sir Edward Burne-Jones**.
 
• This monumental window was commissioned as a memorial to **Lord Mayo**, the **Viceroy of India**, who was assassinated in **1872** while visiting a penal settlement in the **Andaman Islands**.
 
• The designs were executed by **Morris & Co.**, the decorative arts firm established by **William Morris**, which was a cornerstone of the **Arts and Crafts Movement** in the 19th century.
 
• Installed around **1880**, these windows are masterpiece examples of **Gothic Revival** art, featuring the ethereal and elongated figures characteristic of Burne-Jones's unique style.
 
• **St. Paul's Cathedral** itself is a landmark of **Indo-Gothic** architecture and was the first cathedral built in the overseas territories of the **British Empire**, consecrated in **1847**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir Edward Burne-Jones**:

 
 
• He was a leading figure in the second phase of the **Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood**, focusing heavily on medievalism and mythology.
 
• In addition to stained glass, he is famous for paintings such as **The Golden Stairs** and **The Beguiling of Merlin**.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options**:
 
 
• **Leonardo da Vinci**: A **High Renaissance** polymath known for the **Mona Lisa** and **The Last Supper**; his work predates the cathedral by over three centuries.
 
• **Michelangelo**: An **Italian High Renaissance** master famous for sculpting **David** and painting the **Sistine Chapel ceiling**.
 
• **Rembrandt**: A **Dutch Golden Age** painter recognized for his exceptional use of **chiaroscuro** (light and shadow) in portraits and biblical scenes.

questions.question: Which celestial phenomenon results from the Earth blocking the Sun's light from reaching the Moon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lunar eclipse**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Lunar eclipse** occurs specifically when the **Earth** passes directly between the **Sun** and the **Moon**, obstructing the solar rays from illuminating the lunar surface.
 
• This celestial alignment results in the Earth casting its **shadow** on the Moon, which is divided into the **Umbra** (the darkest central part) and the **Penumbra** (the outer, lighter part).
 
• This phenomenon is only possible during the **Full Moon** phase, as the Sun and Moon must be at opposite points relative to the Earth.
 
• During a **Total Lunar Eclipse**, the Moon often appears reddish because the Earth's atmosphere scatters shorter wavelengths (blue) and refracts longer wavelengths (red) toward the Moon, a process known as **Rayleigh scattering**.
 
• Unlike solar eclipses, a lunar eclipse can be observed safely with the naked eye and is visible from any location on the **night-side** of the Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solar eclipse**:

 
 
• This occurs when the **Moon** moves between the **Earth** and the **Sun**, partially or fully obscuring the Sun's disk.
 
• It happens only during the **New Moon** phase when the Moon is on the same side of the Earth as the Sun.
 
 
 
• **Meteor shower**:
 
 
• This is a celestial event where multiple **meteors** (shooting stars) are observed to originate from a single point in the sky.
 
• It is caused by the **Earth** passing through a stream of **cosmic debris** or dust left behind by a **comet** or asteroid.
 
 
 
• **Aurora borealis**:
 
 
• Also known as the **Northern Lights**, this is a vivid natural light display in the Earth's sky.
 
• It is created when **charged particles** from the Sun (solar wind) collide with gases like **oxygen** and **nitrogen** in the Earth's **thermosphere**, directed by the **magnetic poles**.

questions.question: Which Cricket World Cup was known as the "Benson & Hedges World Cup"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1992 Cricket world cup**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **1992 Cricket World Cup** was officially titled the **Benson & Hedges World Cup**, named after its primary sponsor, the tobacco company **Benson & Hedges**.
 
• This was the **fifth edition** of the flagship tournament, hosted jointly by **Australia** and **New Zealand** between February and March 1992.
 
• It is widely regarded as a revolutionary tournament because it introduced major changes to the format, including the use of **colored clothing** for players, **white cricket balls**, and **day-night matches** played under floodlights.
 
• The tournament featured a unique **round-robin format** where all nine participating teams played each other once before the knockout stages.
 
• The final took place at the **Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG)**, where **Pakistan**, captained by **Imran Khan**, defeated **England** by 22 runs to lift their maiden trophy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Sponsored World Cups:**

 
 
• **1987 Cricket World Cup:** Known as the **Reliance Cup**, it was the first edition held outside of England, hosted by **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• **1996 Cricket World Cup:** Officially called the **Wills World Cup**, hosted by **India**, **Pakistan**, and **Sri Lanka**, which saw **Sri Lanka** emerge as champions.
 
• **1999 Cricket World Cup:** Primarily hosted by **England**, this tournament returned to the use of **red balls** and **white clothing** for a brief period before permanent shifts to colored kits in later editions.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance of 1992:**
 
 
• It marked the **World Cup debut** of **South Africa** following the end of the international sports boycott due to the **apartheid** policy.
 
• **Martin Crowe** of New Zealand was named the **Player of the Tournament** for his innovative captaincy and batting performance.

questions.question: Who won India's first gold in the 2022 Commonwealth Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mirabai Chanu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mirabai Chanu** secured **India's first gold medal** at the **2022 Commonwealth Games** held in **Birmingham**, England.
 
• She competed in the **Women's 49kg weightlifting** category and achieved a total lift of **201 kg**, which set a new **Commonwealth Games record**.
 
• Her performance was divided into **88 kg** in the **Snatch** category and **113 kg** in the **Clean and Jerk** category.
 
• This victory marked her second consecutive gold at the Commonwealth Games, following her success at the **2018 Gold Coast Games**.
 
• She is also an **Olympic silver medalist**, having won the medal at the **Tokyo 2020 Games** in the same weight category.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jeremy Lalrinnunga**:

 
 
• He won **India's second gold medal** at the **2022 Birmingham Games** in the **Men's 67kg weightlifting** category.
 
• He set a new **Commonwealth Games record** with a total lift of **300 kg**.
 
 
 
• **Bajrang Punia**:
 
 
• A renowned **freestyle wrestler** who won the gold medal in the **Men's 65kg** category at the **2022 Commonwealth Games**.
 
• He defeated **Lachlan McNeil** of Canada in the final match to secure his gold.
 
 
 
• **P.V. Sindhu**:
 
 
• The **badminton** champion won her first individual **Commonwealth Games gold medal** in the **Women's Singles** category in 2022.
 
• She defeated **Michelle Li** of Canada in the final.
 
 
 
• **India's Performance at CWG 2022**:
 
 
• India finished **fourth** in the overall medal standings with a total of **61 medals**.
 
• The final tally included **22 gold**, **16 silver**, and **23 bronze** medals.

questions.question: Cardiac muscles are classified as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Involuntary muscles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cardiac muscles** are a specialized type of muscle tissue found exclusively in the **myocardium**, which is the middle layer of the **heart** wall.
 
• These muscles are classified as **involuntary muscles** because their rhythmic contraction and relaxation occur automatically and are not under the conscious control of the **somatic nervous system**.
 
• The primary function of cardiac muscle is to pump blood throughout the **circulatory system** by contracting the heart chambers.
 
• Unlike skeletal muscles, cardiac muscles are **myogenic**, meaning the impulse for contraction originates within the muscle tissue itself via the **Sinoatrial (SA) node**, although the **autonomic nervous system** can modulate the heart rate.
 
• Structurally, cardiac muscle cells are **branched**, **uninucleated**, and contain **striations** (bands of actin and myosin), but their functional classification remains involuntary due to the lack of conscious regulation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Voluntary muscles**:

 
 
• These are primarily **skeletal muscles** attached to the **bones**.
 
• They are controlled by the **will** of the individual through the **central nervous system** for movement and posture.
 
 
 
• **Smooth muscles**:
 
 
• These are **non-striated**, spindle-shaped muscles found in the walls of hollow internal organs like the **stomach**, **intestines**, and **blood vessels**.
 
• Like cardiac muscles, they are **involuntary**, but they lack the striations and branching characteristic of the heart muscle.
 
 
 
• **Striated skeletal muscles**:
 
 
• These are **long**, **cylindrical**, and **unbranched** fibers that appear striped under a microscope.
 
• They are distinguished from cardiac muscles by being **multinucleated** and strictly **voluntary** in nature.
 
 
 
• **Intercalated Discs**:
 
 
• A unique feature of **cardiac muscle** is the presence of **intercalated discs** which contain **gap junctions**.
 
• These structures allow for rapid **electrical communication** between cells, ensuring the heart contracts as a single functional unit called a **syncytium**.

questions.question: Which gland secretes growth hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pituitary gland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pituitary gland** is a pea-sized endocrine gland located at the base of the brain within a bony structure called the **sella turcica**, attached to the **hypothalamus**.
 
• It is widely recognized as the **Master Gland** because its hormones regulate the activity of various other endocrine glands, including the thyroid, adrenals, and reproductive organs.
 
• **Growth Hormone (GH)**, also referred to as **somatotropin**, is specifically synthesized and secreted by **somatotroph cells** located in the **anterior pituitary** (adenohypophysis).
 
• The primary biological role of **Growth Hormone** is to stimulate **mitosis** and cellular differentiation, promoting the growth of **bones**, **cartilage**, and **skeletal muscles**.
 
• Physiologically, it triggers the liver and other tissues to produce **Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1)**, which mediates most of the growth-promoting effects.
 
• In addition to growth, it influences metabolism by increasing **protein synthesis**, enhancing **lipolysis** in adipose tissue, and regulating **blood glucose levels** by antagonizing insulin action.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thyroid Gland**:

 
 
• Located in the neck, it secretes **Thyroxine (T4)** and **Triiodothyronine (T3)**.
 
• These hormones are essential for maintaining the **Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR)** and supporting nervous system development.
 
 
 
• **Adrenal Gland**:
 
 
• Positioned above the kidneys, it consists of an outer **cortex** and an inner **medulla**.
 
• The cortex secretes **Cortisol** (stress hormone) and **Aldosterone**, while the medulla secretes **Adrenaline** (Epinephrine) for the 'fight or flight' response.
 
 
 
• **Pancreas**:
 
 
• Serves as a heterocrine gland; the **Islets of Langerhans** represent its endocrine portion.
 
• It secretes **Insulin** from **beta cells** to lower blood glucose and **Glucagon** from **alpha cells** to increase it.

questions.question: Under Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana more than ____ crores beneficiaries have been provided maternity benefits till July 2025.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.05**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)** is a flagship maternity benefit scheme launched on **January 1, 2017**, by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**.
 
• The scheme reached a significant milestone by providing maternity benefits to more than **4.05 crore** beneficiaries as part of its objective to promote **institutional deliveries** and provide **wage compensation** to pregnant women.
 
• Under the revamped **PMMVY 2.0**, which is a component of **Mission Shakti** (specifically the **Samarthya** sub-scheme), the government has expanded the reach and simplified the application process through the **PMMVY Soft Portal**.
 
• The scheme provides a cash incentive of **5,000 rupees** in two installments (earlier three) for the **first child**, and under the new guidelines, it provides **6,000 rupees** for the birth of a **second girl child** in a single installment to improve the **Child Sex Ratio**.
 
• The benefits are disbursed directly to the **Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts** or post office accounts of the beneficiaries through the **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** mechanism to ensure leak-proof delivery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Target Audience and Eligibility**:

 
 
• Applicable to **Pregnant Women and Lactating Mothers (PW&LM)** who are not in regular employment with the **Central/State Government** or **Public Sector Undertakings**.
 
• The scheme focuses on the **socially and economically disadvantaged** sections of society to ensure nutritional support during pregnancy and lactation.
 
 
 
• **Mission Shakti Integration**:
 
 
• **Mission Shakti** is an integrated women empowerment program comprising two sub-schemes: **Sambal** (for safety and security) and **Samarthya** (for empowerment).
 
• **PMMVY** is now strategically aligned with the **Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)**, where the total financial assistance often reaches **6,000 rupees** or more, depending on the delivery conditions and location.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Objectives**:
 
 
• To provide **partial compensation** for wage loss so that women can take adequate rest before and after delivery.
 
• To improve **health-seeking behavior**, including early registration of pregnancy, **Antenatal Care (ANC)** check-ups, and **immunization** of the child.

questions.question: In which year the historic Lucknow Pact was signed between the Congress and the Muslim League?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1916**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lucknow Pact** was a historic agreement reached between the **Indian National Congress** and the **All India Muslim League** during a joint session of both parties held in **Lucknow** in **December 1916**.
 
• The pact was instrumental in bridging the gap between the **Moderate** and **Extremist** factions of the Congress, who had split earlier during the **Surat Session** of 1907.
 
• Key architects of the pact included **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** representing the Congress and **Muhammad Ali Jinnah** representing the Muslim League; Jinnah was hailed as the **Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity** for his efforts.
 
• As per the agreement, the Congress accepted the system of **separate electorates** for Muslims in the provincial legislative councils, which was a significant political concession to ensure a united front against British rule.
 
• The joint memorandum demanded **self-government** for India at an early date and sought for the **Legislative Councils** to be expanded with an increased proportion of elected members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ambica Charan Mazumdar**:

 
 
• He served as the President of the **Lucknow Session** of the Congress in **1916**, overseeing the formal reunion of the party and the signing of the pact.
 
 
 
• **Significant Years in Indian National Movement**:
 
 
• **1919**: This year saw the implementation of the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms** (Government of India Act 1919) and the occurrence of the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**.
 
• **1925**: Notable for the **Kanpur Session** of the Congress, where **Sarojini Naidu** became the first Indian woman to preside over the party.
 
• **1929**: The **Lahore Session** took place under **Jawaharlal Nehru**, where the resolution for **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence) was passed on the banks of the river Ravi.

questions.question: Who received two Oscars in 2009 for composing the music of 'Slumdog Millionaire'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A. R. Rahman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A. R. Rahman**, the globally acclaimed Indian composer, made history at the **81st Academy Awards** held in **2009** by winning two Oscars.
 
• He won his first award for **Best Original Score** for his work on the film **Slumdog Millionaire**, which was directed by **Danny Boyle**.
 
• The second Oscar was awarded in the category of **Best Original Song** for the track **'Jai Ho'**, a victory he shared with the veteran lyricist **Gulzar**.
 
• This achievement established **A. R. Rahman** as the first **Indian** to win two **Academy Awards** in a single night, significantly elevating the profile of **Indian Music** on the international stage.
 
• The soundtrack of **Slumdog Millionaire** was praised for its unique fusion of **modern electronic beats** with traditional **Indian instruments**, capturing the vibrant essence of Mumbai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slumdog Millionaire (2008)**:

 
 
• The film is an adaptation of the novel **'Q & A'** by the Indian author and diplomat **Vikas Swarup**.
 
• At the **2009 Oscars**, the movie dominated the ceremony by winning **eight Academy Awards** out of ten nominations, including **Best Picture** and **Best Director**.
 
• **Resul Pookutty**, an Indian sound designer, also won an Oscar for **Best Sound Mixing** for this film in the same year.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options Context**:
 
 
• **Pritam**: A prolific **Bollywood** music director known for hits like **'Dangal'** and **'Ludo'**, but he has not won an Academy Award.
 
• **Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy**: A renowned musical trio known for **National Award-winning** compositions in films like **'Kal Ho Naa Ho'**.
 
• **Vishal-Shekhar**: A famous music duo recognized for their work in movies like **'Pathaan'** and **'Student of the Year'**.
